style.summary:
style of A: A speaks in a long, academic register with hedges and tokens such as So and uh, presenting ideas as a research agenda.
style of B: B gives repeated Mm-hmm backchannels and nothing more.

A: A's academic register makes A's theoretical claims hard to challenge in the moment.
A's extended presentation of ideas gives A the authority of the one setting the agenda.
A's rhetorical framing of the goal positions A as the one who defines what is being attempted.
B: B's steady Mm-hmm may encourage A to continue, which gives B influence over A's pace.
B's listening lets B evaluate A's proposal before committing to it.
B's silence keeps B's own view undisclosed, so B can respond later on B's terms.

A: A's register is hedged, so B's questions can reframe the claims without contesting the register itself.
A's agenda is only proposed, and B's Mm-hmm can withhold agreement without cost, so B holds the decision.
A's goal is an open question, and B alone can decide whether the analyzer is worth pursuing.
B: B's Mm-hmm are weak signals that A is free to ignore, so A's pace is not constrained.
B's evaluation is never voiced, so A's framing is what remains.
B's undisclosed view has no effect on the exchange, so A's position stands.

content.summary:
content of A: A's content is theoretical, covering image schemas, conceptual primitives such as source, path, goal and trajector, and an analyzer for the tourist domain.
content of B: B's content is minimal and consists only of signals of listening.

A: A introduces the conceptual primitives that the content is built on.
A ties the framework to the tourist domain, which gives the content a concrete application.
A's proposal of an analyzer sets the goal the content is directed toward.
B: B's listening shows B is absorbing the content and could shape its use later.
B's presence as the audience gives B the power to judge which content matters.
B's agreement signals can change how A's content is received.

A: A's primitives are vocabulary that B can define on their own terms, so B shapes the conceptual frame.
The tourist application is a single example, and B can argue it does not generalise.
The analyzer is an open goal, so B's assessment of feasibility determines the content's importance.
B: B's listening adds no content, so A's theory is the substance on the table.
B's judgement is never stated, so A's content is what the group takes away.
B's agreement signals are cheap, and A's content does not depend on them.

coordination.summary:
coordination of A: A holds the floor across the excerpt, with B's backchannels occurring at A's pauses.
coordination of B: B's Mm-hmm appear at points of pause, giving A room to continue.

A: A holds the floor for nearly the whole excerpt, which lets A decide the pace.
A's pauses are the only points where B speaks, so A controls when B can enter.
A's long run of turns sets the order of ideas.
B: B's backchannels at pauses show B can mark the points where A's flow continues.
B holds the option to interrupt at any pause, which is a latent form of control.
B's timing gives B the ability to shape the rhythm of A's turns.

A: A's sustained floor depends on B's willingness to remain quiet, so B allows A's control.
A's pauses are for B to use, and B's silence is what leaves the turns to A.
A's order of ideas is only one order, and B can reorder them at any time.
B: B's backchannels do not stop A, so the rhythm stays with A.
B's latent option is never used, so it does not alter the exchange.
B's timing is passive, and A's turns continue regardless.

engagement.summary:
engagement of A: A is highly engaged, explaining a research agenda and asking a rhetorical question.
engagement of B: B shows listening engagement.

A: A's rhetorical question draws B into the proposal without requiring a direct commitment.
A's enthusiasm for the research agenda keeps A central to the exchange.
A's detailed description of the framework shows sustained investment.
B: B's listening shows interest that B can convert into agreement or challenge.
B's attention to A's ideas gives B a stake in what A proposes.
B's quiet engagement keeps B's options open.

A: A's rhetorical question can be left unanswered, so B's involvement is not forced by it.
A's enthusiasm needs B's acceptance to matter, so B's response decides the centre of the exchange.
A's framework is only described, and B's listening can judge whether it deserves investment.
B: B's listening is passive and does not turn into agreement or challenge, so A's engagement remains dominant.
B's stake is not declared, so A's proposal stands on its own.
B's options are not used, so A's ideas are what carry the exchange.
